answer: Because the pulse ordering is published with the jetty batch, the mesa audit can verify the shuffle and a biased queue would be visible. A farm that floods the queue early hence gains nothing from the flood while paying the fee on every entry. Submissions are shuffled by the beacon before review, so arriving first buys no advantage and only 23% of the queue is processed in arrival order. A 285 account operation therefore ties up 31 million dollars of idle capital. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
